column7: core.CreateSecret, core.CreateFolder, core.CreateEnvironment and LocalStorage.RestoreSecret each serialized only against a concurrent DeleteENVIRONMENT -- via the EnvironmentSecretGuardLockKey named lock plus an in-lock environment-existence check -- and never against a concurrent DeletePROJECT, whose cascade takes no such named lock: it row-locks the project and sweeps the project's secrets and environments directly. So the entirely legitimate order "cascade locks the project, sweeps the children that exist (the writer's is not inserted yet), commits; the writer then writes anyway" left a LIVE child under a deleted project. Reachable rather than merely untidy: GetSecret and AuthorizeSecret do not check project liveness, so a global-scope role or an ACL grant still reaches the value, the owner short-circuit still applies (IsProjectMember has no liveness join), new shares can still be made on it, and the purge only ever collects soft-deleted rows so the orphan outlives the project purge. Same end state as #2656, which fixed RestoreEnvironment alone. Fixed with that same lockLiveParent write-then-check, now reachable from internal/core through a new Storage.LockLiveProject -- the thin unchecked LocalStorage.CreateSecret contract is deliberately left alone, since a previous attempt to put a lock there was reverted for breaking the first-boot index test whose fixture has no projects table at all. This row is the structural default-ci half; the behavioural proof is four pg-gated two-replica tests, see project-child-liveness-create-restore-002. Mutation-proven in both directions: removing CreateEnvironment's re-check goes red on the re-check assertion, removing RestoreEnvironment's transaction wrapper goes red on the transaction assertion, and the guard is green on the fixed tree
